text: The report proposes PMF competition as an explanation for efflux–flagellar cofitness because both use PMF, but notes shared dispensability could produce the same signal.
quote: The PMF competition model would explain why efflux genes correlate with flagellar genes (both use PMF) — but shared dispensability could produce the same signal.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report cites Eckartt et al. (2024, Nature) as identifying compensatory mutations targeting the same functional pathway as the resistance mutation.

heading: Literature Context

text: The report regards organism-specific AMR support networks as consistent with compensation integrating AMR genes into existing organism programs.
quote: Our organism-specificity finding is consistent with this: compensation integrates AMR genes into whatever programs the organism already has.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report cites Nichols et al. (2011, Cell) as showing that condition-dependent fitness profiles reveal gene function in Escherichia coli.

text: The report cautions that functional enrichment in cofitness neighborhoods can reflect shared laboratory experimental context rather than biological co-regulation.
quote: The general principle holds, but our analysis highlights a caveat: functional enrichment in cofitness neighborhoods can reflect shared experimental context (lab conditions) rather than biological co-regulation.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report claims to provide the first pan-bacterial mapping of AMR co-fitness neighborhoods across 28 organisms.

text: AMR cofitness neighborhoods are enriched for flagellar motility and amino acid biosynthesis, although the report cautions that shared laboratory dispensability rather than mechanistic co-regulation may explain this.

heading: Novel Contribution

text: InterProScan GO annotations transformed a null AMR cofitness enrichment result into a significant result, which the report interprets as showing legacy annotations are insufficient for functional genomics.

heading: Novel Contribution

text: The report generalizes that experimental dispensability may cause artifactual co-regulation signals in cofitness studies of laboratory-grown organisms beyond AMR.

heading: Novel Contribution

text: The report cautions that flagellar and biosynthesis enrichment in AMR cofitness networks may reflect shared dispensability under Fitness Browser laboratory conditions rather than mechanistic co-regulation.

text: The report describes AMR genes without antibiotics, flagellar genes in shaken liquid culture, and amino acid biosynthesis genes in supplemented media as metabolic burdens under Fitness Browser experimental conditions.

text: The report states that a permutation test matched on mean fitness level rather than just conservation is needed to resolve the shared-dispensability confound in AMR support networks.

heading: Limitations

text: High cofitness implies shared fitness phenotypes, not direct transcriptional co-regulation.
quote: Even without the dispensability confound, high cofitness implies shared fitness phenotypes, not direct transcriptional co-regulation.
heading: Limitations

text: The AMR cofitness computation replaces missing fitness values with zero in z-score space using np.nan_to_num, approximating but not equaling pairwise-complete Pearson correlation.

quote: For the relatively dense FB matrices this is unlikely to affect conclusions.

text: Broad GO terms such as transmembrane transport and membrane appear in nearly all AMR support networks and genomes, potentially masking specific signals.
quote: Broad GO terms (transmembrane transport, membrane) appear in nearly all support networks and all genomes, potentially masking more specific signals.

text: At |r| > 0.3, AMR support networks average 233 genes and include many weak associations, requiring confirmation at |r| > 0.4.

text: The absence of an AMR network-size–fitness-cost correlation may reflect insufficient variance in fitness cost across genes.
quote: The absence of a network-size-cost correlation may reflect insufficient variance in fitness cost across genes.
heading: Limitations

text: The 28 Fitness Browser organisms are lab-adapted, phylogenetically biased toward many Pseudomonas, and ecologically limited.
quote: The 28 organisms are lab-adapted, phylogenetically biased (many Pseudomonas), and limited in ecological diversity.
heading: Limitations
